body: Caine held his breath as the wind rushed by his ears. He was falling, toes pointed down, arms extended at his sides with his Spellstorm pistols tightly gripped, one in each fist. Below him, he saw only cloudbanks—a billowy swirl underlit by flashes of luminous green. Ace was practically on top of him, also falling. Watts and Ryan were next, similarly posed on either side, Anastasia, then Kell completing his circle out in front. He felt them as much as saw them, reaching deep for his Gift. He focused on a point below, as deep into the cloudbank as he could reach. Next, he opened the space between spaces, felt its cold on his face, and pulled them all through. First Jump They were in the clouds now. Wind still rushed past Caine’s ears as the cloud pressed in, an impenetrable fog. He felt the first tingling of butterflies in his stomach as his descent began to acquire speed. His team was still an invisible presence all around him still, though only Ace’s bulk was easily seen. Again, he looked down, focusing on his Gift. In his mind’s eye, he reached beyond, as far as he could.

name: Name
body: "Fek sake," Watts quailed from over Caine’s shoulder, an age-old fear of heights now put to the test. Caine would not be distracted, holding his focus where it ought to be: beneath the clouds. Once more, he pressed to open the space between spaces, this time feeling a slight resistance. Nevertheless, it shuddered open, and he saw clear sky beyond. Second Jump The night sky beneath the clouds was anything but dark. A hellscape metropolis yawned wide beneath Caine now. In all directions he could see endless towers, great halls with spiked accents, lattice bordered roads, trammeled brass rail lines crossed with overgrown aqueducts, and a labyrinth of sheer walls crawling with black vines. At the heart of the city, he saw an enormous sepulcher of blackest obsidian: a sprawling complex of interwoven domes and spires that could only be the fabled Black Temple. Adjacent to it, another fortress climbed high enough to pierce the clouds—a colossal weave of metal and bones that could only be Toruk’s citadel. And a proper dragon’s lair it was, indeed.

name: Name
body:
Skell presented a full assault on Caine’s senses, but none were so strong as its smell. The flare of his nostrils caught a rising, sulfurous odor—in essence, the dragon blight that tainted this land. The cityscape was lit by green fire in a network of torches, great burning pyres and tall geysers of a luminous pitch that burst forth from their pipework at random intervals. He saw patches of darkness checkering the terrain, shadowy unused spaces, still-water reservoirs, and great open pits that yawned without bottom so far as he could see. To what end? He did not pause to wonder, only to adjust course for ideal terrain. Securing their drop zone was the first priority, and he probed the rushing landscape for the nearest candidate.
He felt the strain of his Gift this time yet peered ahead. He saw a darkened yard a short distance away, one within reach. Towers of scrap were piled high, with narrow footpaths threaded between. A junkyard?
"Fek sake!" Watts repeated, this time louder. He had caught a bad gust in their second appearance and was suddenly sent flailing.

name: Name
body: Caine felt Ryan reach out to steady him as his boot came around… "Look out," Ryan warned but not soon enough. Watt’s boot caught Caine in the ear, knocking him off-balance. He sprawled in freefall, focus lost. "No," he snarled. They were gaining momentum—too much, he knew. They must jump, but he could only glimpse the way now. He pulled the space between spaces wide once more, this time under great strain. He heaved, and the void grudgingly obliged. They were through. Third Jump "Hold on," Caine shouted over the howling wind. The ground was rushing up now, a labyrinth of jagged edges, shadow, and green fire. It was tangled, terrifying, and coming up too fast. Ryan had grasped Watts on the other side, pulling him back into formation. Bailoch and Anastasia did likewise, pushing through the air to grasp each other by the wrists around Caine. Yet the damage had been done. They had achieved terminal velocity. Caine could not cancel momentum between jumps. It would propel them through the next, inevitably fatal fall if unchecked. Split seconds yawned wide before him, the city coming faster.

name: Name
body: "Hell of a way to die," Bailoch glowered. There was one chance to solve it, but the strain would be immense. Caine needed more than focus; he needed to recover. Time was not on his side, but he took all he had. Beneath his toes, the ground had become a horrifying rush only a dozen yards away. "Steady," Caine shouted over the wind, taking a final breath. "Allister…" Anastasia gasped, eyes wide and transfixed on the ground. Caine pried open the space between spaces open again. Below, he saw the clearing where he would land them amidst the tangle of a scrapyard. Yet he knew it would be no simple jump this time. He gathered his focus, wrestling with the aperture of the jump itself, inverting it as ever he must, pulling it round and over his head, all while struggling to keep the actual position in focus. The effort was almost more than he could bear. He gritted his teeth, eyes rolling back of his head. Fourth Jump Mere inches from the ground, Caine and his squad erupted from out of nowhere, turned completely upside down. Flung now to the sky by their carried momentum, they rose with furious speed—twenty yards high, then forty in moments. Yet gravity ebbed their momentum; their climb slowed. Fifty yards high now, Caine and company approached a headstand standstill. Caine had only time enough to look down at a bewildered Ace and shrug. Around him, his crew gasped, so strange their predicament. Caine took a deep breath as gravity began to tug them earthward again. Then…

name: Name
body: "Steady," Caine repeated, closing his eyes. Fifth Jump Caine emerged from the void at a near stop, inches over the ground and at the center of the clearing. His toes touched down, light as a feather. Nearly overcome by the effort, he fell to a knee and gasped for air. Yet his pistols were trained, sweeping round. In support, his team took their places, each with little more than a soft hop. "Holy Morrow," Watts gasped, weapon raised at Caine’s left. "Let’s never do that again," Ryan agreed, sweeping a corridor right. Ace took position behind Caine, weapons ready, as did Bailoch and Anastasia. The old sniper’s rifle was trained on high, sweeping from tower to tower in a full circle. "Clear," Kell said finally, lowering his rifle. "I know that was a rough time folks." Caine swayed, letting his guns drop. "But I’d be much obliged if one of yeh could help me up." ***

name: Name
body:
Cynthia pried at the lock. Her arm snaked out of the cell door window, coming around with her stolen key. The angle was off, and she struggled for leverage. Over and over, she tried to fit the key but missed time and again. Meanwhile, the slim window’s press-metal frame was sharp edged, cutting her arm the harder she tried. It didn’t matter. Deneghra had given her a one-hour head start, and she intended to use every minute of it.
Could she truly escape this place? Her mind raced at the thought. Maybe not. It didn’t matter. After what she had seen, she would be happy enough to die trying. She would not give Deneghra what she wanted, that much was sure. Nor was she going to end up like Elise, either. Even now, fleeting impressions of the lost girl’s tragic final moments haunted her, turning circles in her head, ones she couldn’t shake. They were part of her now.
Then, the key was in the lock.
Though Cynthia’s fingers shook for the effort, she managed to turn it. When it clicked open, the heavy lock fell to the floor with a thud. She had to cover her mouth to keep quiet. Beyond her narrow corridor, she could hear the sisters at work. They were arguing again, this time over who should retrieve their next victim from the pen downstairs. Cynthia held her breath, waiting for them to register the sound of her escape, but it did not come.

name: Name
body:
She opened her door.
She allowed herself a brief smile; after all, this was her element. Years as a pickpocket on the mean streets of Bainsmarket had taught Cynthia how to be quiet, how to move unseen. Though tempted to use her Gift of Magic as well, she resisted, fearing it would be felt. It didn’t matter; she didn’t need it. Not yet. She crept to the edge of the corridor like a mouse, using the corner as cover. Next, she peered around it to watch the hideous sisters at their work.
While Sekka stretched a skin over a drying rack in the corner opposite, Lynek was stamping for the door. It seemed she had lost the argument in the end. She was growling and huffing her discontent between wet coughs as she went. Sekka snorted at her while pausing to admire the stretched face looking back at her from the rack.
Cynthia winced at the sight but dropped low, aiming herself for the near side of the large workbench central of the sisters’ shop. Sekka would not see her there, and if she timed it just right, she could follow Lynek out the door. Lynek was soon gone, the door swinging back. Cynthia moved fast and silently, aiming to follow. Until Lynek returned.

name: Name
body:
At the last second, Cynthia heard the sister’s return to the door. She threw it open and hurled abuse at her gloating sister. She would have seen Cynthia in plain sight but for the fact that Cynthia had already ducked out of sight on the far side of the work bench. Yet her movement did not go entirely unseen.
"What is it now?" Sekka hissed.
"Quiet yourself." Lynek was not amused, scuttling for the work bench with her odd tripod’s gait.
Cynthia saw her coming and looked for an escape route. The only direction she could go was toward the pipe organ chamber. Though her gut churned at the thought, there was no time for anywhere else. She ducked behind a barrel and then on to an adjacent bench and behind another of the sisters’ hideous racked skins left to dry. She heard Lynek coming, her metal feet scraping the floor.
"Is that?" Lynek traced Cynthia’s trail with a sniff, her cowled head cocked.
"Have you lost your mind, sister?" Sekka taunted yet looked away from her work, curious.
"I smell what I smell." Lynek hesitated. She seemed to have a premonition, turning for Cynthia’s corridor.

name: Name
body:
Cynthia blanched as the witch-sister turned on her third heel and scuttled back for her cell. She watched her go, desperate now. She turned for the doorway to the pipe organ and ducked inside the grand chamber. She wasn’t sure there was a way out, but at least the organ seemed large enough to hide in.
"Gone!" Cynthia heard the bitter howl of Lynek from the end of her cell’s corridor. "She is gone!"
"Find her," Sekka hissed, angry. Cynthia could hear her scuttle through the workshop . "She could not have gone far."
Cynthia searched the great chamber. Few hiding places beyond the organ and no exits that she could see. She scanned the walls, seeing no vents or panels.
"I smell her," Sekka called to her witch-sister Lynek with a hacking rasp.
"The organ," Lynek replied hysterically. "Hurry, sister!"
When Cynthia looked to the ceiling, her eyes were drawn at once to the pipes of the organ, extending beyond the ceiling like a great corded tree trunk. There was a gap. She saw a place she could squeeze through, if she could just get there. Hand over hand, Cynthia began to climb as quietly as she could.

name: Name
body:
"Come out!" Sekka was suddenly at the doorway back to the workshop, her cowled eyes glowing like hot embers as she scanned. In her human-looking hand, she brandished her jagged skinning blade.
Lynek next burst past her sister, scuttling into the chamber like a racing crab. Her many arms coiled and tensed reflexively, ready to strike.
Cynthia looked down from the pipework over the great organ, keeping out of sight as best she could. She hid behind a pipe and held her breath.
"Come to us. Do it now." The witch scanned the room, her wretched voice trying hard to sound calm. "We will spare you the worst of our punishments."
Sekka advanced to the base of the organ, inspecting its many nooks at ground level with care. Gradually, her gaze climbed to the ceiling, forcing Cynthia to scuttle around to the side of her pipe like a cornered squirrel. She slipped as she did, forced to stifle a gasp and avoid a fall. In the moments of silence that followed, she feared the worst.
"She’s not here," Lynek concluded, bitter and coughing.

name: Name
body:
"Are you sure?" Sekka raged, looking about to be sure. "You smell her as I do?"
"It lingers, aye," Lynek hissed. "She could be anywhere by now. You let her out after you."
"No, I didn’t!" Sekka hissed, though her protest faltered.
Cynthia watched the pair, silent.
"Would you rather tell our master that," Lynek offered, "or just get her back?"
Sekka resigned. "I will skin her for this myself."
As the pair turned for the door, Cythia swallowed, scrambling for the ceiling. She pulled herself between the ceiling and the pipe, a handhold at a time, into the room above. Almost immediately, she felt sick to her stomach.
***

name: Name
body:
"Don’t stop," Caine warned, running past a thrall as its head exploded into black ichor and gory chunks. His squad was at his heels as another thrall came turning the bend in the path ahead. Caine ran headlong at the thing as it dropped its bundle of scrap to meet him. His Spellstorm pistols were safely in hand, but he did not fire. In fact, he did not even bother to aim. The thrall meanwhile raised powerful fists to meet his headlong charge with a necrotite-fueled tackle. It did not get the chance. Instead, its head burst, just as had that of the thrall before it. And the one before that.
Caine and his newly renewed Hellslingers were running the maze of the junkyard now, closing in on a factory tower to their east, still some two hundred yards distant. To the south, a rail line held a procession of automated carts paused alongside the yard, dumping a load of scrap and proceeding down the track. The night sky was meanwhile a luminous green overhead, lit by torches throughout the yard and a towering pyre at its center. The thralls were like worker ants around them, carrying away what parts could be salvaged. Everything else was methodically hauled by a circle of towering cranes that fed the pyre one bucketload at a time.

name: Name
body:
There were other hazards here, but Kell Bailoch had them covered.
From his perch atop the cupola of the nearest crane fifty yards back, Bailoch’s presence was already paying dividends with an impressive tally. At each turn, Caine paused for direction, waiting for Bailoch’s rifle to cover the appropriate path. Indeed, the dour sniper’s aptly named and magically enhanced long rifle Silence had already dropped fourteen thralls that had chosen so poorly as to cross Caine’s path.
Caine now paused at a T-junction corner, turning to find Kell’s watchful eye upon them, redirecting their movement to the right. So it went, junction by junction, with Bailoch finding the path of least resistance, leading them onward to an abandoned factory at the edge of the yard. Here they would set their rally point. When at last they had secured the location, Bailoch would abandon his perch to follow them in.
For the moment, there was still plenty of ground yet to cover. Caine’s breath came short and rapid, his pace nearly at a sprint. Visible over the heaps of scrap they traversed, a wide throughfare could be seen coming up, with a large workforce of thralls and helljacks dismantling what appeared to be a shipwreck. The obstacle of the thoroughfare was more than Bailoch could handle, and he said so with an upraised hand gesture.

name: Name
body:
"Ace, you’re up." Caine turned to the warjack, directing it to take the lead. The nimble Ace nodded and overtook Caine with long strides. As Ace moved ahead, the umbrella of its cloak shimmered into action, rendering it little more than a smudge in the night air. Caine darted within the field’s influence, followed by his team. In short order, they stepped carefully into the open and crossed the thoroughfare without being seen.  On the other side, Caine signaled a pause, and Ace lowered his cloak.
From his new position, Caine could now see that the factory complex adjacent to them was completely abandoned, crumbling and overgrown with a strangling black weed. It was also separated from the junkyard by a sheer stone wall. He looked down the length of the wall for an approach.
"There." Anastasia pointed from his side, indicating creeper vines on a section of the wall. "We can climb those."
"That’s fine. But we’ll need to open the gate for Ace on the other side." Caine indicated a sealed gate large enough for Ace to enter farther down the wall.

name: Name
body:
So it went, another hundred yards and nine headshots to the wall. Ace meanwhile split off, heading for the gate. At the height of their ascent, Caine slipped over the summit, piling headfirst into a broken window of the factory tower, finding only shadows and silence inside. Whatever the factory’s original purpose had been, the only thing certain now was that it had sat idle for a long time. Thick dust and cobwebs coated the work floor before him, and the shuffle of his feet echoed into wider chambers beyond.
Satisfied that they had indeed found their rally point, Caine helped his teammates inside one by one before giving Bailoch the all-clear. The old sniper wasted no time, moving like someone half his age with his rifle slung and knife in hand. He slipped down from his perch to run the maze, following his own breadcrumb trail of thralls.
When at last the Hellslingers were reunited inside the factory, Anastasia called them over to a workbench where she had unfolded a parchment, using a candle to reveal it was a worn map of Skell with several  areas left to speculate upon. Bailoch hung back, keeping watch at their window.

name: Name
body:
"We’re here." She pointed at one of the blank spots, tracing a wide circle. "Best guess anyway."
Ryan looked over the map with a frown. "Why so many uncharted areas?"
"This map was drawn by a slaver captain operating out of Five Fingers." Anastasia shrugged. "It was the best he could make out from his few approaches. What’s important is where he brought his slaves to be offloaded. That’s one of two places Cynthia could be."
"Where is that?" Watts pulled his bare chin.
"Here." Anastasia traced a circle over a wide area east of their position with markedly better notation. "This structure along the river processes all prisoners on arrival. Over here, the triple tower of the warwitches. Seeing as the witches serve at the bidding of Deneghra, there’s a good chance Cynthia may have been brought here instead."
"As long as we can get close to her," Caine said, "I should be able to sense her. The harder she’s takin’ things, the easier I reckon it’ll be."
"We could always hitch a ride." From his place at the broken window, Bailoch hearkened to the sound of the track’s steam whistle as the latest cargo of scrap was unloaded into the yard by the automated rail carts. "That line down there runs east, more or less."

name: Name
body:
Caine left the map to join Bailoch, followed by Anastasia, Watts, and Ryan. He observed the track, his gaze following the elevated line as it led east. Then he looked to the junkyard and the trail of bodies they had left behind.   "A fine tally." Caine smirked. "Too bad I ain’t paying you by the head here, chum."
Bailoch scoffed.
"There isn’t much time." Anastasia rolled up her map, replacing it in her scroll case as she regarded the train. "It’s getting ready to depart."
"You heard the lady," Caine nodded. "Let’s move it."
***

name: Name
body:
"Cynthia," a woman’s voice sobbed.
Cynthia stopped in her tracks, squeezed between sweating brass pipes that twisted and tangled their way to and from the chamber overhead. Had she heard what she heard? She squinted up. She could begin to see the room like a galaxy of stars in a great metal amphitheater. She could not believe her eyes, so brilliant was the view.
Yet there were yards of pipe in her way still. She resumed climbing, unsure of her feelings. What was certain was pressure building against her temples coupled with nausea. This feeling, she understood, was because this place was where the souls went. She agonized to think how many times she had heard the witch sisters play their foul organ. What it meant.
But that voice?
She gritted her teeth and climbed, pulling at a loose wire to heft herself up and onto a riveted brass floor. She turned over like a cat on all fours, scanning for trouble. When it did not come, she collapsed, gasping and rolled over to stare up at the ceiling, wide-eyed and horrified.

name: Name
body:
The "stars" of this galaxy were souls, each one cradled in tiny soul cages that hung from a great curved brass ceiling. The whole of the chamber projected the aspect of a diving bell over thirty yards across. Some cages hung on short chains, unreachable, up into the dome of the ceiling. Others were suspended on long chains that hung nearly to the floor. All slowly swayed as if in a slight breeze. Some cages tinkled against each other, adding to the eerie aspect of the scene. The pipes of the soul organ emerged center of the floor, angling all directions. Amidst them rose a curving brass-railed stairwell fifteen yards high, with an obscured platform above, positioned dead center of the room.
She glanced at the platform, sensing a presence there—strong, but jumbled. Confused? She looked next at the walls, finding double doors that appeared to be the only exit. Overhead, she saw small, circular hatches along the ceiling like the port windows of a steamship. The atmosphere here felt heavy. Every sound was magnified, resonant. Her head lightly throbbed as she struggled forward.

name: Name
body:
Ahead, a low-hanging soul cage held a single light, a swirling orb exactly like the others…yet somehow different. Cynthia felt compelled to touch it. When she did, the little girl Elise was on her mind, a ghostly vision of her final moments.
You can’t be here, a voice suddenly echoed frantically in Cynthia’s mind.
She recoiled, pulling her hand back. As she did, Elise vanished from her thoughts.
Gingerly, she reached out again, feeling the cold brass surface and Elise both. "I’m so sorry, I…I mean, what they…uh, for what happened to you."
Cynthia could feel a bottomless sorrow emanating from within the soul cage.
"I mean, I almost…ate you." Cynthia shook her head, then grew angry. She grabbed the metal cylinder containing Elise’s soul, snatching it from the chain. "No. I won’t let them have you. We’re both getting out of here."
Inside the cage, the floating soul pulsed brighter, urgently, as if compelling Cynthia to flee.
"Cynthia," A woman’s voice called down from atop the platform. "I know you’re there, darling. Please come where I can see you."

name: Name
body:
There was no mistaking it this time: It was her mother. Cynthia felt her presence for an instant, clear, unmistakable. Then, a sense of murk returned, the feeling of something other.
Elise radiated urgency, and Cynthia’s mind was bombarded with images of the door.
"But I have to see," Cynthia explained, cradling the soul cage. "I’ll be quick."
She was true to her word, darting up the curved stairs to find an arcane device atop a wide iron-grated platform plucked straight from a nightmare. It was a soul cage, larger than any other. Its design was a lattice of riveted iron big enough for a person and shaped like an iron maiden. There was a padlock keeping the device locked tight. Within it, Cynthia saw a ghostly vision of her mother struggling against her prison.
"Darling," her mother sighed. "Let mummy out."
"Mama," Cynthia rushed to her side, horrified.
Yet as Cynthia reached a hand to her mother’s spectral cheek, her mother’s image instantly withered, revealing a ghastly visage. What remained was no less than the mocking face of her father’s alter-ego, the terrible pistol wraith. It laughed at her dismay, an ugly rattling sound that echoed through the chamber.

name: Name
body: Cynthia jumped back, a squeal escaping before she could cover her mouth. "I’m sorry, my darling. He won’t let me see you." The wraith again spoke with her mother’s voice, then blinked. To all appearances, the wraith seemed to struggle with itself. She noticed a table beside it with several of the creature’s effects laid out, including a timepiece and a pair of spectral Spellstorm pistols. "You can’t be here." Cynthia shook her head. "Allister killed you!" The wraith was distracted, snarling. Yet it was not looking at Cynthia. The baleful embers of eyes looked now at the stairwell. Cynthia followed its gaze, and there she could see Deneghra ascending, a sneer spreading over her cold dead face. "Foolish child." Deneghra smiled. "My wraith shall rise again each time I summon him." "No." Cynthia stepped back. She glanced to the rail of the platform and saw a dozen grisly guards in support of the witch sisters at the door. If only she had heeded the warnings from Elise. "An impressive escape." Deneghra stepped close, still smiling. "I knew you had potential. Yet why run when you could now save your mother?"

name: Name
body: "I don’t understand." Cynthia looked between Deneghra and then to the long fall to the floor over the rail of the platform. "Each soul my wraith takes remains within him." Deneghra laughed, an ugly sound, placing her hand over the cage in front of the wraith’s luminous forehead. She lingered that way, runes forming around her hand to draw out a tiny ball of soft white light from the creature. It seemed as though Deneghra was plucking the very thoughts from her hideous creation. Cynthia noticed a curling tendril of gossamer light tethering the wraith to the tiny orb. In fact, he seemed unwilling to let go. The specter snarled in defiance, and Cynthia saw something like a tug of war begin. The wraith gnashed its teeth, hissing. The orb began to retreat within him the more he did. Deneghra was not amused. "We’ve been over this," she insisted, and the runes swirling over her hand flared, their intensity soon becoming a blinding light. "She is… not…. yours." The effect was immediate. Deneghra’s magic was antiseptic, leaving her spectral minion to recoil in agony. It howled a tortured dirge made all the more unnerving by the chamber’s amplifying acoustics.

name: Name
body:
"You see, child?" Deneghra smiled, extinguishing her magic. Indeed, the show of force had neatly severed the Wraith’s gossamer connection. As she looked closely upon it, her corpse face was softened by its light. "Your mother is here."
Cynthia watched Deneghra turn the globe over and again in her hand like a busker’s sleight of hand, hypnotized as it leaped and dipped to the warwitch’s touch. Could it really be her?  She blinked, looking back to the defeated wraith. The ghastly creature appeared for all the world to be gasping for breath it did not need and convulsing with pain it should not feel.
"What’s wrong with him?" Cynthia looked on in morbid fascination. "Why did he fight you for her?"
"He was trying to save her." Deneghra looked from the soul in her palm to the humbled wraith with contempt. "Do you believe that?"
"Save her?" Cynthia was angry. "He killed her."
"His mind is a twisted tangle, as I have made it," Deneghra explained. "As with your true father, he regarded your mother as a lost love. Sorely missed, even. Yet to my wraith, death saved her. In taking her soul, he thought them reunited, happily ever after."

name: Name
body: She paused, a distant memory seeming to interrupt her thoughts, but she just as quickly dismissed it. "Pathetic." The wraith growled softly at Deneghra’s scorn, anger creeping back over the pain of her torment. "Does he think I’m…his daughter?" Cynthia shook her head, trying to make sense of what she was hearing. "As much as he can," Deneghra said, shrugging. "You ask what is wrong with him? He is a Caine. Perhaps that is the sum of it." "Just what is that supposed to mean?" "Understand that no wraith has ever been forged of a warcaster before. I’ve long been curious to try. The lure of your father’s gifts was irresistible, I admit. He did find you, after all. But his temperament exasperates me. It truly does." "Temperament?" Cynthia shook her head again, regarding the stricken wraith with an increasing sense of disbelief. "It seems an Allister Caine of any shade is destined to disobey. Yours, mine…it matters not. It’s simply who he is." Deneghra sighed. "Well, I’m afraid it just won’t do. It is time to put this Caine down once and for all. Right after I have squeezed out every last soul from within him."

name: Name
body:
The wraith hissed again; his smoldering eyes locked with Deneghra’s.
Cynthia winced at the death sentence then looked again to the soul floating softly over Deneghra’s palm. If she could just get Deneghra to talk a little longer, an opening might appear…
"Yes," Deneghra seemed to sense her thoughts, holding the soul out to be taken. "Save her."
"How?" Cynthia struggled. Her hand reflexively reached out for her mother’s soul yet stopped short of taking it. She waited for Deneghra’s answer with dread. In truth, she knew the answer even as she asked the question.
"Consume her of, course." Deneghra laughed. "That is the only way now."
***

name: Name
body:
"Everyone out!" Caine saw the claws coming down first and raised a hand in warning. The enormous articulated arms that the claws were attached to towered over the open-topped rail cart like a colossus reaching for them, casting a foreboding shadow. While they were meant only to lift their cart and rotate it for loading, Caine and his companions were unfortunately still inside of it.
The procession of carts had entered the bowels of a fully operational necrofactorium, leaving them surrounded by enemies on all sides. Caine knew to disembark, even for an instant, would mean exposure from every angle. Under the many lights, scaffolds, and crowded workstations of a wide open and vertical interior fully four stories tall, there was neither room nor cover to engage Ace’s stealth to any real effect. He shook his head as his feet hit the ground. There was nothing to do now but fight. At last…
It would not be the first time Caine would have to think of a plan on the fly, not by a long shot. As he landed in a crouch by the tracks of the factory floor, he saw a milling workforce of mostly blighted trollkin before him, their reactions a mix of surprise and anger. His hand was forced—the one thing he knew for certain in that moment was that there could be no survivors. With that in mind, he got straight to work.

name: Name
body:
He opened fire into the crowd of oversized humanoids, aiming each shot with care. In their leather coveralls and thick, scaly hide, he knew them to be famously tough and was sure to make each shot count. So, to each of his victims, a headshot. Beyond the press of trollkin he saw even more ghastly, zombie-like thralls as well, many emerging from the catwalks and scaffolds that overlooked the work floor space. Before him, Caine saw what the necrofactorium was designed to produce: enormous hulking machines—wraith engines—were lined up in four bays across from him, still incomplete and sagging in their harnesses. Little mercy there, as he counted scores upon scores more workers converging upon them.
Behind Caine, the Hellslingers followed his lead with a vengeance. Bailoch aimed quickly and shot a thrall from a high scaffold overhead, pausing just long enough to watch the wretched creature fall silent at his feet before scrambling up the ladder to the fourth-floor position to take its place.

name: Name
body:
Watts and Ryan sprang into action on either side of Caine in a fury, channeling maximum damage into their spell-fire with glittering rune halos and thunderous reports. The result sent the surviving trollkin diving for cover, and Caine blasted a pair to ruin before they could find it.
There were helljacks here, too. Slower to react, a pair now joined the firefight, leaving their patrol routes to come at Caine’s crew with flexing claws. Beside him, Anastasia scanned the chamber, looking for an angle.
"We’ve got to get out of here," she said, reverting to Llaelese in frustration.
"We need to bring the house down besides." Caine groused over a reload then opened a fresh volley at a charging trollkin. The spine and scale-studded thing was coming at him with an enormous wrench, yet it died at his feet with half its head gone. "Anyone but us makes it out, we’re as good as made, darlin’."
"A difficult proposition, but not impossible." Anastasia scanned the high vertical workspace. "Look."
"Ace!" Caine was distracted from impending death and guided his warjack to intervene as the first helljack closed on their circle with its great clawed hands outstretched.

name: Name
body:
Without delay, Ace intervened ahead axe-first to sweep aside a raking claw then shot the helljack point-blank in the face. Its slender-necked cannon blinded the thing at once, yet a flurry of axe blows were required to force the enemy to stagger back.
With room to move and a blind target all but helpless to defend itself, Ace reloaded. Next, it leveled its cannon for a second rune-shot and fired. The luminous glitter-laced eruption blasted the helljack’s metal carcass backward, though there would be no time to gloat, as the second helljack was fast approaching to take its place. It vaulted over its fallen comrade to join the fray, sprinting to close the gap before Ace could reload a third time.
The odds of survival were falling fast, and Caine knew it.  As he turned from Ace to Bailoch, Watts to Ryan, indeed every angle beyond his circle, he saw reinforcements arriving to the din of the battle. Finally, he glanced at Anastasia’s focus on high—time enough for a glance and no more as Ace squared to meet the second helljack.

name: Name
body:
Anastasia was pointing to a fourth-floor balcony, and Caine saw a row of great ironbound wooden silos there. As far as he could make out, each silo was marked with symbols for a variety of raw materials used in the factory floor production line below. He saw an assortment of sizes and markings but nothing so useful as a good powder keg.
"That one." Anastasia redirected Caine’s attention, reaching for her satchel. A thrall shot through the mid-section fell two stories, landing at her feet. She kicked the skull-faced thing in the teeth until it stopped clawing for her. "It’s sodium."
"Sorry," Bailoch called down, reloading his rifle.
"What about it?" Caine squinted at the silo Anastasia indicated even as he continued firing into a crowd with more thralls piling in.
Ace had been engaged by the second helljack only a few yards away, the pair now locked in a chaotic swirl. Caine blinked as he saw the helljack close enough that Ace was forced to defend a torrent of blows with his axe alone. Denied the space to use his rune-cannon, Ace was suddenly in serious jeopardy.

name: Name
body:
"Gonna get yerself wrecked like that, chum." Caine diverted focus from the fourth-story silos just long enough to compel Ace back, imparting a portion of his Gift to his warjack’s rune-carved cannon for good measure.
Ace responded, his light frame managing a clever zigzag, yet the helljack would not be denied, surging after him. Caine growled at the thing’s impertinence, diverting a single Spellstorm shot with a touch of thunder for maximum impact. He fired with a resounding bang just as Ace found room enough to level his barrel a third time.
Caine’s shot struck true with a resounding bang, knee-capping his target. The helljack’s advance ended in a tripped up, face-first tumble to the ground, claws flailing out before it. As was always their bond, Ace was ready.
Caine’s warjack set the muzzle of its rune-carved cannon squarely between the fallen helljack’s balefire eyes and fired before it had time to get back up. The resulting spectacle of boosted spell-fire burst the helljack’s metal skull into white-hot fragments. In short order, the massive, jagged claws stopped flailing, and the warjack’s signature death-rattle of venting steam began.

name: Name
body:
With a breath of relief, Caine stepped back of the helljack’s wreck to focus on the silo Anastasia had indicated. "You were saying?"
"Sodium," Anastasia repeated, pointing high. Next, she indicated another silo directly below it on the third-floor catwalk. "Chloride there, right underneath it. Big mistake."
"Do they go boom?" Caine resumed fire, finding two thralls closing on Watts at his left. "Tell me they go boom."
"Oh, they do." Anastasia smiled. "With a pretty big acid cloud besides."
"Sounds like good cover." Caine grinned. "I like this plan."
"Good." Anastasia sidestepped a rushing thrall. She put a blade in its eye then pushed it clear to fall to the floor. "Of course, I hope we’re long gone when that happens."
"Noted." Caine grimaced, seeing the rail cart they had just bailed from being set back onto the track by the enormous mechanical arms, now loaded with a row of three newly built helljacks secured in harnesses and set in the space where his team had been stowaways only moments before.

name: Name
body:
"Fek me," Watts sighed at Ryan as she sent a charging trollkin back with a deafening report. As a thrall came hissing toward her, he dropped it with a point-blank rifle shot to the face.
"Nice save," Ryan acknowledged, still firing.
"What’s the play?" Anastasia looked above the skirmish, still fixated on the fourth-floor silos.
"Watts, Ryan," Caine paused shooting, watching as the great yard arm paused over the rail car behind them, "hold tight. We’ll be back."
"Sure, boss." Watts shrugged, capping a trollkin between the eyes before turning to Ryan. "See that?"
"I did." Ryan ducked back as Ace cleaved a thrall in half alongside her. "Take your time, boss. We got this."
Caine smiled as he drew on his Gift, opening the void for himself and Anastasia. He brought them through, appearing atop the mighty claw of the industrial arm as it retracted for the ceiling. It was an uneasy landing, forcing his attention to maintain even footing.
"Hold on," Caine warned, taking Anastasia under his arm while grappling the yard arm’s piston for balance. "Fourth floor, going up!"

name: Name
body:
The pair began to rise on the back of the yard arm. Caine watched as it neared the end of its traverse, then he pulled Anastasia into another jump, this time adjacent to the fourth-floor silo. Bailoch saw them appear and immediately fired at a target over Caine’s shoulder. Caine turned to see Bailoch had killed again, this time a bloated creature with spindly limbs moving in on them on four mechanical legs and slashing with jagged claws mounted on metal poles.
"Necrotechs," Bailoch shouted across the gap. "They’re coming out of the woodwork now."
Caine nodded then turned back to Anastasia. He watched as she drew two charges from her satchel and began to crank clockwork timers on each.
"Five minutes?" Anastasia held a charge out for Caine, indicating an arming button.
"Five minutes," Caine repeated, holstering a pistol to take the device in hand. "This one on the chloride?"
"Yes." Anastasia showed him her device, pointing to the arming button. "You got a plan to get us out of here before then?"

name: Name
body:
"The track." Caine looked down at the track line that ran through the center of the factory floor. "I reckon we follow it out."
"That, or we find something that acid won’t dissolve and get under it." Anastasia shrugged. "The secondary blast is going to spectacular."
"Got it." Caine started. Another necrotech had found them, leaping from the shadows between silos with a gleaming claw aimed at Anastasia’s shoulder. The creature slashed her cloak, drawing a line of blood beneath it and eliciting a scream. As she ducked away, Caine fired a pair of shots that sent the creature flailing back, dead. Then, to his confusion, the floor shook. A horrendous caterwauling could be heard below, along with the groan of metal being torn.
"You all right?" Caine helped Anastasia up.
"I’m fine." She turned to look over the rail. "What was that?"
Below them, a massive wraith engine on the factory floor had activated, coming loose from its harness. The enormous death machine was thrashing around the floor, unable to hover, one-armed and incomplete but somehow functioning. The answer to that mystery was solved as Caine saw more necrotechs on the factory floor, scrambling between the three remaining wraith engines still in their harnesses.

name: Name
body:
"Tricky bastards." Caine watched his team dance away from the unfinished monstrosity’s single claw, firing round after round to no effect. Ace too was driven back, unable to contend with the size of the thing. "It’s getting hot down there."
"Then let’s get out of here." Anastasia placed her charge then hit the arming switch. "Meet you at the track?"
"You got it, darlin’." Caine winked then pulled himself through a solo jump to the third floor, right next to the chloride silo.
There was movement close, so he didn’t linger. Instead, he set his charge and looked out over the rail. Below, his squad continued to evade the rampaging, half-built wraith engine. Unable to hover as designed, it chose instead to drag itself toward them. Caine was dismayed to see two more of the nightmare machines had now been activated and were struggling against their harnesses as an increasing number of necrotechs worked to free them.
They were running out of time, charges or no charges. Any longer and this fight would be unwinnable. Caine reached back to activate his charge then looked to Bailoch at his perch on the fourth floor.

name: Name
body:
"Kell," Caine shouted. "We are leaving! Rally at the track."
The scar-faced sniper nodded, squeezing off one more shot into the factory floor brawl. Then Caine saw a shadow looming behind Bailoch, moving in fast—too fast to stop, though he tried.
"Look out," he shouted, raising a pistol.
A necrotech lunged from the shadows. One of its long claws plunged into Bailoch’s side before he could get clear. He groaned, sagging to the attack.  Caine took the opening to fire a shot. The necrotech was killed instantly, but the damage had been done. Bailoch struggled on the ladder, bleeding from the attack. Caine pushed himself across the vertical space, leaping to receive Bailoch on the third floor as he descended the ladder.
"He just nicked me." Bailoch registered Caine’s arrival with defiance, though he did not refuse an arm for support. Then, Caine focused again, bringing them both to the factory floor behind Watts, Ryan, and Ace.
"Fall back," Caine looked to the track’s exit of the factory. "Let’s go."

name: Name
body:
"Thought you’d never ask." Watts backpedaled from an advancing wraith engine, avoiding its claw by inches.
As they ran the line, Caine helped his wounded sniper. He looked ahead, finding the track exited the factory at a pair of double doors a dozen yards ahead. Thick double doors blocked the way, latched with a durable spring mechanism to open them. The latch trigger was not in sight.
"Fek," Bailoch muttered as they reached the doors. Caine tried to push them open as the seconds ticked away but to no avail. He needed a stronger touch.
"I’ve got a dressing." Anastasia arrived from shadow, her gaze at once on their wounded sniper.
"Ace." Caine pulled his backpedaling warjack’s attention around as it hacked at the nearest wraith engine, pointing to the doors. "Have at it."
Ace clanged to the affirmative, turning from the infernal machine to take three steps into a charge. It raised its axe high and slashed the latch open easily. At once, the doors sprang open, and the Hellslingers moved to escape into the humid night air beyond.

name: Name
body:
Then, the first charge detonated.
Caine and company braced for the shock of the blast then looked up. High overhead, the blast had ruptured the fourth-floor silo and much of the surrounding floor, sending white powder spilling to the factory floor in a cascade. The workforce left behind them was stunned, looking up in confusion at the deluge. Yet Caine knew the next charge would end them all if they didn’t get clear.
"Time to go." He pointed to the open doorway even as three wraith engines tried to drag themselves closer, claw by claw. They hissed and leaked, struggling but determined.
"Stay put, why don’t yeh?" Caine backpedaled out of the door as the last Hellslinger escaped. He meant to get in one more, but it proved unnecessary. As the second charge detonated, the wraith was consumed, lost to sight. Caine’s world became fire.
***

name: Name
body:
"Fool of a girl," Deneghra laughed. "Did you think there was another way?"
"Fek yourself," Cynthia snarled, beyond tired, beyond caring. "I’ll never take a soul. I won’t do it!"
"Then watch as I do." Deneghra narrowed her eyes, all humor lost.
Cynthia recoiled, horrified. Deneghra began to pry the ball of light in her hand apart, grasping it as though a ripe piece of fruit, pulling…
"Stop it!" Cynthia screamed, leaping to intervene.
Deneghra was ready for her, backhanding Cynthia to the floor of the platform without missing a beat. As Cynthia fell, she watched Deneghra resume her grisly display, biting her mother’s soul and tearing it with her teeth. As she did, Cynthia heard a faint screaming—and by degrees, it grew louder. A luminous vapor suddenly spilled out and Cynthia felt more than heard her mother silenced.
In an instant, the vapor of her mother’s essence was inhaled by Deneghra, its light extinguished. Conversely, Deneghra’s pallor suddenly grew warmer, her features softening. For a moment, she seemed almost…alive. A light grew in her eyes, bright and green. Behind her, a shadowy pall appeared from nowhere. All light in the chamber instantly seemed blotted away, and tentacles of inky blackness began to radiate from behind Deneghra, twisted and coiling. She guided a pair of them forward, questing for Cynthia, easily encircling her with a grip like ice.

name: Name
body:
"So good." Deneghra exhaled luminous vapor, exultant. Then the pall of shadows was gone, the tentacles of shadow banished to nothing.
"You’re a monster." Cynthia sat stunned by the vile act, gasping for air. Her heart was racing and yet broken at the same time. The room seemed to sway around her. She had nothing left.
"I thought you had potential. I see now I was wrong." Deneghra looked down at her, her radiance fading fast as the disgust in her words turned her face to a snarl. She waved down the witch sisters to join them on the platform. "Take her. Put her in the box."
"I don’t think so." Cynthia wiped a tear, but her expression rapidly hardened. In an instant, she knew how to kill the warwitch, though it might well kill her, too. She reached for the key in her pocket and, at last, called upon her Gift with iron determination.
Deneghra sensed the change, reaching for her. Cynthia simply rolled clear of Deneghra’s grasp. In the split seconds of her movement, she sensed a shortcut through space itself was right there, her instincts screaming she need only open the door. As she reached with her Gift, a shadow tore reality itself open to receive her. At once, she knew this was the space between spaces, the very same void her father traveled.

name: Name
body:
The coldness of the shadow struck her like a winter’s chill as she slipped through. On the other side, she emerged to find herself beside the pistol wraith’s soul cage. It turned suddenly at her approach, confused. Without hesitation, she set Deneghra’s key into the rune-carved padlock, leaning close to the creature for a whisper. In a fluid gesture, she took up its pistol from the table adjacent.
"Kill her." Cynthia was pitiless, her eyes locked to the wraiths as she held its pistol. "Kill them all."
The lock was open. The wraith erupted from its cage with an unholy shriek. It took the weapon from her hand in a blur and wasted no time using it. Deneghra was caught off-guard, struck immediately with an ugly blast that opened her throat. She gurgled her shock, ichor spraying wildly from the wound, yet raised the arcane defense of her power field. Still the wraith fired, two more shots weakening the incandescent bubble even as it formed, driving her back. Still, she found focus enough to counter, launching a searing bolt of magic at the wraith as she fled the platform. It merely jinked to avoid her attack, firing another shot to drive her back.

name: Name
body: Cynthia saw the wraith would not be stopped now nor did it seem interested in her. Like an angel of death, it launched itself from the platform, tracing a wide arc through the chamber’s ceiling, navigating the soul cages that dangled all around. It circled, trading shots with Deneghra. She countered as best she could, yet she seemed to be on the back-foot against the creature’s rage. For a moment, Cynthia could only gape at the spectacle. Somehow, she was still alive. When she heard the shouts of the sisters approaching below, she snapped back to reality. From the folds of her rags, she gripped Elise’s soul cage, feeling the girl’s ghostly presence in her thoughts. We’re leaving, she thought, grabbing the pistol wraith’s remaining weapon for good measure. What about them? Elise wondered at the guards still gathered at the door, spreading out to contend with the wraith and still block her escape. "I’ve got this," Cynthia whispered, looking to the open doorway just beyond them. She summoned a shadow and disappeared into it.

name: Name
body:
"We are close to the central paddocks." Anastasia led the way, moving through side streets and alleys that were disturbingly empty. "Do you sense her?"
"No." Caine was frustrated. His entire plan had hinged on being able to sense his daughter. Yet as they approached the foreboding high walls of a complex meant to feed Cryx’s never-ending appetite for the living and the dead, he felt nothing—nothing but a growing sense of dread in the pit of his stomach.
Overhead, a dusting of ash had begun to fall, cast in the soft green of Skell’s pervasive necrotite-fueled torchlights. Caine felt the tropical night air as a humid breeze on his face amidst the softly falling flakes. It was an odd sort of tropical snow, indeed. Behind them, he could hear shouts and confusion even a few klaxon alarms. It was not for nothing.
Behind Caine, a toxic fire raged, and a crowd was growing to watch it. He himself could not avoid looking back at the spectacle of the thing as they pressed forward. The inferno of the exploded factory was spreading still, five-alarm strong and billowing an acrid miasma for blocks in every direction. Though they may have gotten away with little more than singed clothes, there was no denying the advantage of surprise was decidedly lost.

name: Name
body: Forces would be marshalled to determine the cause and eventually to track them down. Caine looked back the way they had come, suddenly aware that even Ace could not cover their tracks in the fresh fallen ashes. Not for the first time, he began to wonder if Rebald had been right. Had he led his team to their deaths? Was Cynthia already dead…or worse? Not so fast. "Hold up." Caine put a hand up to take stock of things, ducking into an alcove. What exactly was the plan now? Keep moving, spread chaos… Caine nodded to himself as his plan evolved. As long as eyes were on the fire, they weren’t on him. Moreover, distraction was a ploy they could continue to stir as they went. He looked up to the high walls again with renewed purpose. Once inside the complex, prisoners themselves would make a very potent distraction. More than this, it would not only keep the enemy busy, it would alert Cynthia… "You got something, boss?" Watts chuckled as he peered around the alley corner, his humor thinly veiled.

name: Name
body:
"Yeah." Caine’s eyes traveled up the side of the looming walls. "Let’s get in there, move fast and stir things up. If we get Cynthia riled, I’m more likely to sense her."
Watts and Ryan turned after Caine paused, their eyebrows raised.
"Does that work for yeh?" Caine asked, snapping the cylinder of his pistol closed with a flick of his wrist.
"I reckon it does." Watts smiled bitterly.
"If you can leap me to that there tower, I expect I’ll be able to cover you as you make your way through the pens." At the end of the alley, Bailoch regarded the prison complex and its nearest guard tower rising fifty yards tall over the high walls of prison.
"Let’s get to it then." Caine led the way, his eyes on the tower.
The Hellslingers followed.
***

name: Name
body:
Deep in the belly of the beast, Cynthia was running for her life.
The labyrinthian corridors of the warwitch temple were a blur, alternating between obsidian façade halls, high vertical chambers lit by hanging torches, and a twisting underbelly of cramped, press-metal corridors with bizarre brass chambers like the one she had fled. There was pipework everywhere and numerous pens where doomed prisoners sat huddled, waiting for oblivion.
There was constant movement here, too, in the form of witches, thralls, deathly guards in morbid armor, and strange machinations she could not name, all with apparent duties to attend. Most disturbingly, many of these were in the process of leading people to their death. She saw now the true scale of an operation that processed human souls for power, as with the grand chamber from before.
Cynthia skirted all of it, emboldened by her evolving gift. As danger presented, she either blended with the shadows or vanished into them entirely. No matter the horrors she saw, she kept moving.

name: Name
body:
She had no idea the conclusion of Deneghra’s quarrel with the wraith, nor did she care. All that mattered was that it had bought her time to escape. At every step, she carried the wraith’s rune-engraved pistol in both hands, ready to use it. She was hesitant to fire the arcane weapon for fear of the noise it would surely make, to say nothing of the fact it had only six bullets in all. It did not matter. If pressed, she would use them all. Moreover, she swore to save the last bullet for herself, if escape proved impossible. They would not do to her what had been done to Elise.
Even as she kept moving, Cynthia knew the witch sisters were never far behind. They were following her, and she couldn’t seem to lose them for very long. At times, the distinct sound of their odd gait echoed in the corridors. At other times, the sobs and hacking coughs of their bickering carried through the vents of the temple’s underbelly. Whatever their means were, they were tracking her. In her mind, it seemed as if they were never more than a few steps away.

name: Name
body: Breathless in her flight, Cynthia needed rest and directions both. Seeing a storage room along the corridor in the citadel’s underbelly, she moved inside, clutching the soul cage to her chest. Elise was in her thoughts again, a spectral voice echoing in her mind. "What do you remember of this place?" Cynthia said as she caught her breath. "When they brought you here, I mean." From back the way they had come, Cynthia could hear arguing. The sisters remained close yet seemed confused. Cynthia’s mind was filled with images of boats, a pier on the bank of a river and whips of slavers—shadowy memories swirling within the essence of Elise, glowing within the soul cage. "Why there?" Cynthia peered around the corner of the chamber to regard the corridor. Elise seemed to shrug in Cynthia’s mind. Escape, a whisper echoed. "Worth a try," Cynthia nodded, feeling Elise’s raw lifeforce in her hand and the warmth it radiated. Again, she had that peculiar taste in her mouth. She swallowed hard against it, looking ahead.

name: Name
body:
"This way, this way," Sekka shrieked as she hobbled along Cynthia’s path.
"Oh, no." Cynthia bolted into the corridor, gripping Elise’s soul cage in one hand. "This way?"
Elise tugged at Cynthia’s consciousness: an image of stairs flashing in front of her vision.
Cynthia rounded the corner, finding stairs just as Elise predicted. They led to the citadel’s ebony upper floors once more—and a host of new problems.  At the top of the stairs, she was surprised by a line of prisoners being led by ghoulish guards through a four-way junction of polished obsidian.
"We can’t go this way," Cynthia warned her spectral companion, ducking back.
Feeling trapped, she turned back down for a new corridor, finding more stairs. In this direction, she could see that the next floor had vista views overlooking the city.
"Maybe we’ll see the docks from here?"
***

name: Name
body:
Elise pulsed excitedly in response.
Cynthia opened a shadow to duck behind an obsidian obelisk as a cruel-looking witch in unadorned black robes surprised her rounding a corner. Next, she ran ahead to find a third-floor balcony overlooking the city’s east side. Large flakes of ash were falling, just like snow. Across the horizon, row upon row of towers and tenements and temples and towers drew a jagged jawline lit by the evergreen glow of necrotite torches. It was an imposing cityscape, the streets below her mostly empty. Unfortunately, there were no docks to be seen.
"Up here, sister. Hurry." Sekka was leading the way, close but out of sight at the bottom of the stairs Cynthia had just climbed.
Ahead, she could see a patrolling helljack ascending another wide stairwell. The nightmare machine walked with deliberate, echoing footfalls, constantly scanning left and right as it went. As she began to sense its thoughts, she dared pad softly up behind it. Where was it going? She felt her Gift come alive the harder she pressed, giving her its sense of a destination; a bridge crossing to meet an adjacent tower. A way out? The warjack turned to her as she read its thoughts and stopped walking. As it raised its clawed hand to grasp her, Cynthia realized her mistake.

name: Name
body:
"I’m not the girl yeh want!" she hissed with as much authority as could be mustered against the comical mismatch of scale. Incredibly the helljack paused, its claw closing to a fist. Then it returned to its route as she gaped after it.
The light of Elise’s soul dimmed, a warning to Cynthia that she should avoid detection.
"Yah, but I know how to get past the guards now," Cynthia whispered to the soul cage, climbing the stairs after the plodding helljack. "There’s a bridge."
"A bridge too far," Sekka rasped, an arcane mist spreading round her hideous tripod legs.
"Too far twofold," Lynek laughed across from her sister with a spittle-doused cough and more of the fey mist in curling tendrils at her feet.
"You couldn’t—" Cynthia was stunned by their appearance. "How?"
"The scent of your soul fills our senses." Lynek grimaced at Cynthia’s confusion. "There is nowhere you can go we cannot track you."
"Now come to your senses," her sister coughed. "There is no escape."
How had they gotten the drop on her? Cynthia recoiled from the closest of the misshapen sisters to find the other scuttling toward her. There was nothing left now but to fight. She gripped her weapon even as magic was swelling in her chest. Sekka lunged, arms flailing, eyes burning with hate from under her cowl. Cynthia jinked, letting the sisters collide. She turned and let spew her Gift in anger at last. It burst from her like a tar vomit, a shadowy gout that doused the recovering sisters, hissing and sizzling with an acrid smoke that burned their twisted forms. Yet they soon laugh-sobbed at the painful black wash, no strangers to torture.

name: Name
body: "Is that all?" Sekka coughed, her metal arms coiling to strike. "Submit," Lynek mocked in sobbing singsong while edging toward Cynthia. "The end will come easier for you." Cynthia leapt back of the sister’s advance, raising her pistol with both hands and a shriek. Two shots, then three, then four she blazed into those that had caused her so much torment. She gave it all back, five shots then— Elise’s voice blazed within the soul cage, stopping Cynthia cold, leaving her breathing hard, the pistol shaking in her hand. Before her, the sisters had paused their advance, realizing along with Cynthia they had not been hit, not even once. Had she missed all five shots? Maybe, maybe not. A faint field seemed to ripple around the hideous creatures as she looked closer. She recalled Deneghra’s power field, and the first few shots the wraith had landed before she could raise it. Again, the sisters proved there was more to them than met the eye. And again she wondered what they truly were. In the end, it could not matter. She was defeated.

name: Name
body: She fell back from the hunchbacked sisters in a panic, tripping flat onto the floor, gasping for breath. The sisters loomed, gloating as their metal arms reached toward her. One shot left… Elise was in her thoughts, resolute, energized. "I can’t do it." Cynthia sagged. Elise was steadfast even as Cynthia faltered. Get up…fight! Too strong, Cynthia thought as the sisters’ shadow fell over her. No… Elise would not let go. Use me. The ghostly words echoed through Cynthia’s mind. Cynthia shook her head, whispering aloud. "There has to be another way." Survive… Cynthia could feel the little soul pleading. All that matters now… Cynthia closed her eyes, resolved at last. As she finally surrendered to her appetite, her grip on Elise’s soul cage tightened. Like a dam burst, Elise was suddenly drawn out in a brilliant light. Cynthia absorbed the radiance of her doomed friend instantly, nothing spared. She shook with its power, a strand of her hair suddenly blanching as she did. She dropped the emptied soul cage, feeling Elise gone from her thoughts.

name: Name
body:
Yet even as her friend unraveled within, Cynthia felt a new swell of magic surging in her own chest. Elise’s gift of essence was fast spreading to her extremities, and her eyes flashed white. She gripped her pistol with renewed strength and plied her gift, easily opening a shadow on the floor next to her. As the sisters lunged, Cynthia rolled into it—and escaped their grasp.
Through the void, she effortlessly turned her exit on its side, her prone position become a wide-legged stance on her feet, positioned as an executioner presiding over the hunched-back sisters final moments. Her pistol felt like fire in her hand yet burned to her touch and not the other way around. She held it firmly to a very surprised Sekka’s temple and pulled the trigger.
"Die," Cynthia said.
The pistol exploded in her hand, or so it seemed. Cynthia perceived time at a crawl, her shot a dazzling burst that erupted like as a rune-laden fireball. The shot spun, scything, burning, unstoppable. Whatever the sister’s ward, it could not stop the raw fury loosed by the little girl they had tormented for weeks on end. Indeed, her final shot burst through the first sister and effortlessly into the next, smashing through the wall behind them, leaving a scorching crater in its wake.  Both heads were utterly ruined with a sudden splash of ichor, leaving their mutilated bodies to sag to the floor, splayed over each other and gone limp.

name: Name
body:
"Well done!" A wounded but unimpeded Deneghra suddenly applauded, delight plain on her pale gaunt features. Behind her came a veritable wall of guards, witches, and thralls. "You are everything I could have hoped for. Let me show you the way forward now."
Cynthia turned to the gloating warwitch, registering the many wounds the wraith had inflicted to no apparent effect. She wondered if there was any stopping Deneghra. Not by her and not in this moment, to be sure. There was an alarm sounding—a series of gongs—from somewhere on the citadel’s upper floors. She considered her predicament as she thought back to the bridge the helljack had shown her. Without hesitation, she turned and ran upstairs.
In a breathless sprint, Cynthia soon found the bridge, a fifth-story crossing to another citadel tower similar to the one she had fled. She dashed across it to find safety but soon realized there were more fiends on the other side. She saw a gathering of thralls and witches. They did not move, did not threaten. They simply stood, all of them, waiting for her. Cynthia stopped midway across the bridge, turning to find Deneghra and her witches blocking her only retreat.

name: Name
body:
"Cynthia," Deneghra raised her hands in a welcoming embrace. "You can never go back to them. You have tasted the power. You’re one of us now."
"I’m not,." Cynthia edged to the side of the bridge, looking down. "I’ll never be."
A steep fall, too far and ending in a stone-floored courtyard. There was an open gateway beyond. She saw the helljack still on patrol, now walking below on the fourth-story bridge just under her. Could she use it? It didn’t matter. She had to try. She stared at the thing, told it to listen to her with her thoughts.
It did.
Cynthia jumped.
***

name: Name
body:
"What the hell was that, boss?" Ryan was at Caine’s face, leaning in close and waving. "Are you all right?"
Caine blinked, finding himself sitting against a wall inside the Cryx prison complex. He wasn’t sure what happened or how he’d ended up here. What he did know was where to find Cynthia.
He sat up, cracking his neck. The dimly lit halls around him were alive with freed prisoners dashing past in a desperate silence. He squinted to the summit of the guard tower, and there he saw Bailoch at work.  Memory of a leap to deliver the sniper there returned. As his team moved between the pens to release prisoners, the old sniper removed guards with surgical precision. To all of their credit, the alarm had not yet been sounded, and half the prison was freed. His memory came flooding back with full force.
"You kind of blacked out there, boss." Ryan still looked over at Caine even as she moved to direct prisoners out the way they had come.
Ryan was clearly not alone in her concern. Ace was looming over him, craning down with a cocked head. Watts was close by, as was Anastasia, both monitoring a corridor to direct traffic while keeping watch for guards on approach.

name: Name
body:
"Ace had to grab you." Ryan thumbed in the direction of the warjack.
"I’m fine." Caine got to his feet. "I finally saw where Cynthia is."
"What?" Anastasia drew near. "You’ve seen her then?"
"Aye. She’s in a pinch." Caine walked up ahead, gaining new bearings as Ace followed. "She’s trying to bust loose. It’s going wrong."
"Where is she?" Anastasia looked the length of the corridor for a stairwell. "What floor?"
"That’s just it." Caine shook his head. "She ain’t here."
Anastasia paled, reverting to her native tongue. "Then where is she?"
"The warwitch temple." Caine closed his eyes, picturing the vision his connection to Cynthia had shown him. Finally, in her darkest moments he had sensed her. "She’s with Deneghra…and she’s…"
"What is it?" Anastasia slipped back into Llaelese, one hand on Caine’s shoulder.
"She’s hurting." Caine broke, furious. "She’s scared. That’s all I know."
"Then we must hurry." Anastasia turned the squad round, keeping her hand on Caine. "We need to go back."
"Tell them we’ve got to go." Caine turned to his squad as freed prisoners continued to open the pens around them. "I don’t expect there’s much chance any of them are getting far, but it suits us."

name: Name
body:
"What about us?" Anastasia returned her knife to its sheath, readying to move. "Do we have a chance?"
"Now that I know Cyn’s alive?" Caine smiled, gesturing up to Bailoch to join them. "We’ve got more than a chance, darlin’."
As his Hellslingers regrouped, Caine led them on a winding course crossway through town, treading over ash-covered streets to the outer courtyards of the warwitch citadel. As traffic increased, Ace covered their passage more and more. Caine was becoming increasingly aware that the fresh fallen ash left their trail in plain sight. It couldn’t be helped. His little girl was close, and she needed him. With every step, he felt it.
As he followed the skyline west toward the triple towers of the warwitch citadel, he delivered his squad to the rooftops for a better look. He came to the nearest ledge overlooking the warwitch’s distinct temple and the complex surrounding it and took a knee to consider it.
As he stared past the arcane shimmer of Ace’s umbrella, he assessed the trio of obsidian towers jutting from a shared stonework foundation. Those towers were surrounded by a maze of courtyards and shrines, each tower connected to the others in a triangular network of sky bridges at intervals of floors. The architecture of the towers was black obsidian with tall steeples; red banners were strung between floors. At the center of the unique structure, Caine could see a fifth-story bridge—and he knew at once his girl was there, desperate to escape.

name: Name
body: Her emotions were distracting his own in turns—raw, primal, determined. "Come on." Caine spurred Ace and his squad to advance, moving for the bridge through the witch’s stonewalled maze of courtyards. Where he could not be bothered to turn the corner, he simply moved his squad to the other side. He would not be stopped now. His girl was here. There was trouble brewing, the closer they got. No doubt about that. Caine saw a flurry of movement on the exposed terraces and along the corridors within. Noise. Guards. But none of them looking his way. He followed the vortex of attention forming around the skybridge he now led them to. There he saw guards forming on one side. Warwitch acolytes. Thralls as well. And there, on the other side, he saw… Cynthia. She ran out alone and in rags, stopping halfway across before encountered the witches blocking her way to the other side. They also came after her, more witches—and the very worst of them all. Deneghra. Victoria Haley’s corpse sister and all-around bitch of a lich harried his girl to the edge yet seemed now to be cajoling her to return. Caine scowled, raising a Spellstorm pistol to iron sights. She was out of range unless he were to take a running start and put a few jumps in. Could he make it? He squinted, building his focus.

name: Name
body:
"Give the word." Bailoch raised his rifle and scoped the looming warwitch.
"Do it—" Caine began, but he recoiled to see Cynthia falling. She had thrown herself to her death rather than be caught.
Caine saw a helljack reaching for her as she fell past the fourth floor. By the scruff of her collar, it had her and gently so. He knew at once she had done it—she was compelling the thing to her aid. He felt both terror and pride in his chest in that moment, but it was short-lived.
From above, Deneghra watched the drama unfolding and immediately took action. She gestured down to the helljack, and suddenly it was reaching out to secure Cynthia, not save her. She reacted with a scream, kicking away from the helljack’s incoming grasp.
"Bailoch, take Deneghra. Do it now."
The old sniper didn’t have time. Cynthia’s rags tore and she screamed to find herself falling again.
Caine wasted no time measuring range now. He started to run straight for her. At a full sprint, he pulled himself through the space between spaces once, twice, three times, forming a trajectory for the place where Cynthia was about to fall. He holstered as he jumped, appearing on the third leap with arms outstretched.

name: Name
body:
Cynthia fell neatly into them a heartbeat later, still screaming. She blinked as they hung in midair, staring into his eyes. Anger, terror, and confusion twisted her features for a moment. Then she buried her head in his shoulder, sobbing in recognition. "Pa."
"Been waiting too long to hear that." Caine smiled, then leapt one more time, straight down. He dropped to the ground softly, taking a knee to kiss her forehead before a rough inspection for wear and tear. She bore plenty of cuts and scrapes in her filthy rags. She was malnourished to be sure, beaten and filthy. But alive. Very much alive. Caine smiled wide before sparing a glance to the shouts overhead.
"Wh…How did yeh?" Cynthia stammered, fighting back tears of disbelief as she looked into his eyes.
"I’ll tell yeh all about it, kid." Caine pointed up at the gathering overhead and Deneghra’s screams to stop them. "Yeh want to get out of here first?"
"More than anything."
***

name: Name
body: 623 AR Merrin Outskirts A babbling brook wound its way through the clearing, alongside which Kapitan Zahara Vilkul’s non-descript black horse-drawn carriage had been parked. The trail leading here was an old loggers’ route abandoned to war and the menace of the Orgoth rush some weeks ago. The loggers had left their timber here unclaimed, great pines stacked in orderly piles along with saws and other tools of the trade. Inside the carriage, Vilkul noted the new arrivals outside her door, closing her scroll case with a deep breath and a clear purpose. "You were right to alert Section 3, Magziev," Vilkul said, throwing back the doors of her coach to exit. Vilkul descended the coach ladder with a piercing glance over her surroundings as the former Greylord Volkova waited in silence. As with Vilkul’s carriage, the cloak and the civilian clothes she wore beneath had been carefully chosen to be completely unremarkable in the company of Ords, and so she had passed among them to arrive here, unseen, hiding in plain sight. It served her calculations, though the time for anonymity was over.

name: Name
body:
Vilkul had chosen this secluded clearing as their place to meet outside of Merrin, just within reach of the Orgoth ruins of such sudden interest. Within these woods, they were out of sight of allied positions, be they Cygnaran, Khadoran, or Ordic. The Orgoth had been driven back for now, yet they were close to the north, no doubt licking their wounds and replenishing their ranks.
For how long? Vilkul would have an answer soon. Her prized warjack Razor and her hounds were already pursuing reconnaissance on that account, circling wide of the loggers’ clearing and staying out of sight of all positions, even those of their fellow Khadorans.  Time was of the essence, she sensed. Yet there were loose threads to attend here first.
Behind the coach, her trusted companion Lazarenko approached the group standing before Vilkul; he was carrying a shovel over the shoulder of his plain grey civilian work clothes. His default squint appraised the new arrivals with only a casual interest as he smoked a cigarette. He looked to Vikul with a single nod.

name: Name
body:
"Thank you, Kapitan." Volkova saluted, watching as the SKS-6 leader stepped down from her coach ladder to address her. Behind the former Greylord stood two of Borisyuk’s men, a downcast and dour sniper and a burly Winter Korpsman, both formed to attention.
"These are the men?" Vilkul looked casually past Volkova’s shoulder.
"Yes, Kapitan. They were in the chamber with Borisyuk." Volkova stepped aside. "They will tell you what they saw."
Lazarenko sidestepped a freshly dug pit behind the men, coming round with soft steps to the right shoulder of the korpsman.
"In fact, I have already confirmed the artifact through another source," Vilkul declared. "These men will tell no one what they saw."
"As you wish, Kapitan." Volkova nodded.
Without warning, Lazarenko swung his shovel round to strike the bull-necked Winter Korpsman next to him on the back of the head, knocking him unconscious. He was felled like a tree, long and straight, into the shallow grave freshly dug for him. When the sniper turned in shock, he looked first to his comrade, then to Lazarenko, and then frantically back around to Vilkul for mercy.

name: Name
body:
He found no mercy with Vilkul—only her pistol aimed at his chest. She did not waste time with pithy remarks; she simply fired. Under the steel blue chill of her merciless gaze, he struggled to stand, then slumped lifeless into the place Lazarenko had dug for him. For good measure, Vilkul fired two more shots into her victims, each to the head. She casually holstered her weapon and pulled upon her chin, her thoughts already seizing upon the next priority in the order of operations.
Volkova raised her eyebrows at the sudden violence but did not flinch. "What about Borisyuk?"
"When the time is right, you will bring him to me." Vilkul again appraised her surroundings, pausing to listen. There—the faint gait of her Razor to the northwest of the wood. They were circling back. Good. "He will need to be debriefed."
"Yes Kapitan." Volkova waited. "Anything else?"
"You may go." Vilkul turned from Volkova to Lazarenko.
For his part, Lazarenko was already covering the men over, heaving shovelfuls of freshly dug earth without breaking a sweat. Her companion puffed a breath of his cigarette, pausing at his work to watch Volkova depart, his eyes narrowing.

name: Name
body:
"You really think they found it?" Lazarenko said to Vilkul.
"Quite sure." Vilkul nodded. "I know that we cannot let Cygnar have it. Not for any price."
Through the woods, the thunder of Razor’s rapid footfalls was inescapable—his gait became a predator’s gallop. His heavy metal frame came in close, circling, watching, seething as his exhaust pipes belched smoke. He approached her, dipping his head low for contact.
Behind Razor, a rough-looking trio emerged from the woods, bundled in dark cloth, tactical body armor, and brandishing vicious assault weapons. These were her Hounds; feral Teterya, dour Fedyniak, and the brute Skrobala. They knew better than to return should their task have been left incomplete. As such, she smiled to their approach, calculating her next steps.
Quieting herself, Vilkul held Razor’s offered chin and soon felt an impression of its travels when it had ranged beyond her ability to maintain a connection. She saw two Orgoth columns, one holding to the north as another moved east on the double. She saw the Cygnaran positions preparing; likewise, the Ords. She then saw the Orgoth ruins and the Cygnaran batteries repositioned in support of the line there. Finally, she saw the river, and the Cygnaran supply depot there. The recovered artifacts had already been packed into crates, neatly bundled for extraction.  Yet the Invaders were not there to carry it all away. They were gone. Vikul blinked at this revelation, restoring herself to the present moment and her surroundings.

name: Name
body:
"Are you not finished?" Vilkul gazed at Lazarenko as he hefted his last shovelful over the dead men.
"Yes Kapitan." Lazarenko smiled, tapping ash from his cigarette as he returned the shovel to his shoulder.
"You three," Vilkul looked to the Hounds. "Tell me what Razor cannot."
"The Cygnarans will be busy." Teteryev chuckled bitterly on approach, lowering her weapon. "The Orgoth now drive two fronts."
"That much Razor tells me," Vikul noted. "The question is where?"
"Coming here," Fedyniak pointed east, "and upriver. They are moving to intercept the flow of refugees from Merrin."
"Oriax will not be denied his harvest it seems," Vilkul agreed, turning to orient herself to the river. "And the Cygnarans?"
"Oh, they’ve taken the bait," Skrobola rumbled. "Rosko in command."
"Extraction of the artifacts would have taken priority," Vilkul contemplated. "She disobeyed orders."
"You said she would." Lazarenko crushed out his cigarette.
"So I did." Vilkul turned on her heel with a satisfied smirk on her face. "And the relic remains."

name: Name
body:
"Everything remains," Teteryev affirmed. "At the field depot, under guard. Packed for transport to a riverboat waiting on the Dragon’s Tongue."
