"There would be complications, if it makes that boat." Lazarenko moved for the back of their coach.
"We are prepared to delay their Invaders a while longer?" Vilkul looked over to Fednyiak.
"We have all the explosives we need," Fedyniak said. "Give the word, Kapitan."
"In due course." Vikul looked down to her civilian clothes, feeling their usefulness at an end. "Lazarenko, it is time to suit up."
Lazarenko was already at the back of the coach, the boot opened to reveal several suitcases of gear stowed. "Yes, Kapitan."
"You know me too well." Vilkul smiled. "That is why we never lose."
***

name: Name
body:
"Gravediggers, drop!" Cynthia ran first down the lowered ramp and into the sky. Pokey came stomping after her, his triple-chute harness secured and triple-checked. Behind her warjack, Baxter’s squad spilled out after, observing the discipline of thirty-yard intervals.
Tumbling into freefall, Cynthia looked up to see a midday sky of blue and her departing Invaders, the Furious Finn and Cracker Barrel now emptied of her platoon. As ordered, they were moving to hold position over the Tague Bridge to drop supplies as needed. With every second, they grew smaller above her as she reached terminal velocity.
Five thousand feet to drop.
Cynthia’s short freefall was slowed by a sudden tug as her pilot chute opened the main chute. Likewise, she looked up to see her fellow Gravediggers blossom their chutes in turn. She looked down to find the ground far below to be vast and silent. Only the rush of wind was in her ears now. She saw the river curve over the landscape, and she followed it along.
Cynthia saw the river met by a wide road and soon revealed a covered bridge. Locals called it the Tague; Cynthia called it the drop zone and began to tug the handles of her chute to adjust course toward it.

name: Name
body:
Cynthia’s orders had been to secure the artifact first, but she had refused to clear the Invaders to go. Not on her watch. There were lives to be saved here, and she needed them both. When her platoon had secured the bridge and stopped the Orgoth advance on the refugees, they would be free to go. Not a minute sooner.
Cynthia felt the usual nausea of impending battle turn over in her gut, yet she fought it easily this time. As she could well see from her high vantage, both her gambit and her refusal had paid off.
The Invaders’ swift flight had allowed the Gravediggers to beat their foe to the punch, and that was going to be half the battle. Indeed, Oriax’s forces were nowhere near as she surveyed the treelines and the fields below. It was a chokepoint the Orgoth warlord would soon regret traveling, if she had anything to say about it.
Cynthia guided her chute ever closer for the bridge, meaning to land the roof itself for a superior vantage. A quick look up and she found Pokey watching her, his triple chute blooming out overhead and his weapons at the ready. Her Gravediggers were fanned out overhead, keeping tight formation and in control. Another hundred yards to go…then, movement.

name: Name
body:
Cynthia saw a scramble in the tree line on the Merrin side of the bridge. Ordic partisans? No. Not Cygnaran and not likely Khadorans, either. She looked with her every sense heightened, drawing her rocket launcher as she fell from the sky.
Then, an eruption of enemy from the woods on the near side of the bridge. Cynthia could see straight away they were Orgoth scouts. No doubt, they had called Oriax to this route. A squad of nine of the vile raiders was moving for the bridge now, fully clear of the woods. In all likelihood, they meant to report back. Cynthia was not about to let that happen. But her rate of fall was painfully slow. Moreover, the raiders saw her coming. Bolt throwers were being raised to her approach—axes as well. She needed the first shot. Fortunately, she knew how to get it.
Caine had told Cynthia all about her rescue from Skell. She was pretty sure he’d embellished it some, but the landing always stuck with her.
Beneath Cynthia’s feet, a shadow opened. She slipped through. Twenty feet below, she appeared, closing the shadow behind her and with it, severing her chute. She was falling now, starting to pick up speed. Then she opened another shadow, aimed her rocket at the center of the scrambling squad and vanished. She slipped through the shadow, appearing fifty feet over their heads. She could hear their shouts of surprise, but it was already too late for them.

name: Name
body:
Cynthia fired her rocket, feeling the rush of its travel to impact. The heat of the blast rose to consume her, but she was prepared. Opening a final shadow, she simply vanished as the glittering blast of her rocket consumed everything within reach. On the other side of the void, she safely emerged to reload, now turned to face her enemy from a safe distance behind them as she dropped to one knee. As she slapped a new rocket into place and raised the iron sights, only a few skirmishers remained, shellshocked and singed in the blast. They tried feebly to come at her but were soon annihilated by her second rocket.
Cynthia celebrated the win with a satisfied nod then regained her footing to look down the length of the bridge. As she did, Pokey fell to earth behind her, quickly draped with its oversized chutes. Then, her Gravediggers began to fall around her, their kit bags hitting the dirt first. In short order, they were cutting their chutes, checking their gear, and falling in.
"You get the next ones, okay?" Cynthia grinned as her warjack loosed its drop harness with a shrug, noting its attention was fixated on the fallen Orgoth skirmishers before them.

name: Name
body:
Pokey banged its fists together in agreement, eager to start shooting.
"Trust me, there’s going to be enough for everyone." Cynthia watched as Sergeant Baxter fell in beside her. "You know what to do, Sergeant."
She indicated positions along the riverbank on either side of the bridge.
"I saw the column," Baxter said. "About a mile out. Looks bad."
"Assume they saw us," Cynthia said, and without another word, she slipped into a shadow to take to the roof of the bridge. From there, she steadied herself and looked out over the farmland vista to the north. Smoke was rising above with the sound of stamping feet.
"What do you see?" Baxter shouted up, watching her survey the horizon.
"A hell of a fight."
"You want me to call a supply drop?" Baxter rummaged for the flares in his side satchel.
"Probably." Cynthia squinted, making out the vanguard of the column. She could just see the warlord Oriax himself astride a massive gharlghast warbeast. The creature thrashed against its handlers, tugging at its thick chains with scathing belligerence.

name: Name
body:
"What do we need?" Baxter looked on. "The Patriots? Ammunition?"
"Just hang on." Cynthia stepped through a shadow, suddenly in front of him. "Let’s see how badly Oriax want this bridge first. Set up firing lines and get ready."
Baxter nodded, replacing the orange flare from to his vest as he looked at the circling Invaders high above. "Aye, Captain."
***

name: Name
body:
"Look there." Vilkul indicated a trail fifty yards south of her elevated position. She knelt in the dirt as she watched a pack of Orgoth skirmishers running ahead of multiple siege tarasks. She counted six of the lumbering beasts in all, with a horde of at least thirty axe-wielding skirmishers sprinting ahead.
"They’re moving to flank the Cygnarans," hissed Teterya as she watched through her looking glass.
"Let them." Vilkul restrained Razor with a stern glance. "It serves us."
Razor was crouched, coiled. The warjack wanted to attack, but Vilkul could not let it. There was work to be done yet. The Orgoth were useful to her cause and must not be impeded. Not at the moment.
"Let’s go." Vilkul let the Orgoth move past then drove her team forward. Before long, they arrived at a thicket in the woods where the Cygnaran position in support of the ruins could be discretely observed. There were fellow Khadorans another few hundred yards down the line—Borisyuk’s replacements by her estimation.
Like leopards, Vilkul’s team stalked, drawing their scopes out for a closer look at the Cygnaran lines. Vilkul observed Gravedigger gun batteries and a nominal force of Ordic militia had been left in defense of the ruins, supported by a trio of warjacks walking a perimeter defense. As she noted, they were Patriots all, each fitted with a long-range sniper cannon to eliminate anything that closed in on the batteries. She granted that the Cygnarans had left behind an effective defense.

name: Name
body:
Yet Vikul noted few Gravedigger artillerymen and a minimum of militia was all that truly remained in terms of manpower. The rest of Captain Rosko’s platoon was gone. Further downrange came the rumble of an incoming horde. She turned her attention to find skirmishers charging through the wood. Danger pressed in on all sides now, yet she had nothing to fear. In fact, it was all going according to plan.
"Look." Skrobola pointed, excited. "They have range."
With shouted urgency, the Cygnaran Artillery Corps were loading their field guns and laying out belts of ammunition for their machine gun nests.
"So they do." Vilkul smiled, turning to Lazarenko. "Shall we set the stage, Lazarenko?"
Lazarenko nodded, and the hounds crept forward. She watched as they bypassed the occupied soldiery and their warjacks alike, setting a charge here, a charge there.
When Lazarenko returned, he was unspooling wire from his charges. He clipped the wire to a primer box and presented his work with a narrow smile. "Ready, Kapitan?"

name: Name
body:
Vilkul nodded, turning to watch as the first of the field guns traversed in their dugout, their firing solutions finally set. "Now, Lazarenko."
As Lazarenko drove the plunger down, a series of detonations rocked the Cygnaran batteries with deep thuds and brilliant flashes. The ground shook, dirt cast up, and one by one, the guns were scuttled. As they emerged from the smoke, the surviving Gravediggers wore panic on their faces, scrambling between the smoke and their splintered weapons. Their trench lines had also been opened by the blast, leaving their position exposed to the enemy.
Meanwhile, the rising din of the approaching Orgoth was undeniable. All that truly remained to challenge them were the trio of Patriots. Among an advancing line of siege tarasks, a mighty gharlghast strode to the vanguard, bellowing a shuddering cry as it came, pausing only to launch rockets from its back. The whistling rockets arced into the trenches, blasting the defending infantry to paste or submission.
Yet the trio of Patriots would not be cowed by the assault, their nerves of steel unfazed, their attention swiftly focused on the mighty Orgoth warbeast. Their guns reported deadly fire, precision shots seeking targets across the massive hulk. Invulnerable as it was, the trio’s relentless still fire found purchase in the chinks of its armor with countless hits. The creature howled frustration, blasted and buffeted but determined nonetheless. It crashed into the first Patriot with a primal fury, driving steel-adorned talons deep into its prey. The doomed Patriot was rent on the spot, easily lifted up off the ground. With an ear-splitting bellow, the titanic beast tossed the wreck into the next Patriot that was advancing, knocking it down and silencing its gun forever.

name: Name
body:
As the Patriots’ defense faltered, the Orgoth raiders shouted their dark praises, cheering ever louder, readying to follow in after it. Vilkul saw the raiders closing in behind their gargantuan beast and smiled.
There was one Patriot still in the fight, and it had no plans to back down.
The lone Patriot was resolved, even heroic, in the lopsided match. It fired its sniper, the round tracing its way to the warbeast’s exposed face. A minor victory—the gharlghast lost an eye, forcing it to stop in its tracks, clutching at the wound with a mournful bellow. Its ammunition exhausted, the stalwart Patriot pressed the advantage anyway, charging with nothing but its trench blade, which it thrust into the soft underbelly of the wounded gharlghast. Despite the small wound, it staggered the gargantuan back one step at a time, the creature’s spidery belly arms flailing to find its attacker. For a moment, it seemed the Patriot might actually drive the Orgoth’s mighty gate crasher back the way it had come and into the woods.

name: Name
body:
Vilkul noted the effect on Cygnaran morale, as the surviving forces of the militia and Gravediggers were regrouping, even lending fire into the oncoming charge. Cheers were going up among them as they fought.
"No, that won’t do," Vilkul said, shaking her head, watching.
Alongside her, Lazarenko had an answer. From the safety of his position, he unshouldered his bazooka and aimed it downrange. Beside him, Teterya loaded the weapon with a slender, needle-tipped shell and tapped Lazarenko’s shoulder.
"Easy," Lazarenko whispered, aiming his iron sights at the lone Patriot. As its back was exposed to him, Lazarenko squinted to find a target on the boiler tank it wore.
He squeezed the trigger, and his rocket hissed a plume across the gap between them in a flash. The warjack’s boiler was at once ruined, erupting in a bright flash of torn metal. Scalding hot water splashed to the ground; all its pressure was lost. The warjack stood motionless, steam hissing from its breached hydraulic system, paralyzed beneath the heaving gargantuan.

name: Name
body:
The staggered gharlghast at once sensed the opportunity and recovered with a bellowing cry, then stomped its massive foot on top of the immobilized warjack, flattening it and removing it from the fight for good.
Lazarenko smiled as Vilkul clapped him on the back.
"The stage has been set," Vilkul noted, standing up from her position. "Let us get to the depot."
***

name: Name
body: Tague Bridge The battle for the Tague Bridge was already underway. The firefight had leveled the roof—what splinters remained either burned or floated downriver. The bridge’s forty-yard length had become a blood-soaked no-man’s land. The bodies of fallen Orgoth raiders now lined its interior while more still floated in the river after spilling over its sides. Yet Cynthia had no time to admire her platoon’s handiwork. What remained of the last wave had made the crossing in the end, bringing the fight up close and personal for the first time. Now she and every Gravedigger who remained were fighting for their lives. Cynthia was knocked aside by a savage ulkor’s axe blade, sent face first to the ground while Pokey ducked between a pair of advancing Jackals just ahead, the trio locked in a brutal melee. Sergeant Baxter wasted no time rushing to her aid, driving his bayonet deep into the red-skinned brute’s ribs before he delivered the killing blow. Around them, her Gravedigger platoon fought back with blade, rifle, and bare hands as both human and inhuman Orgoth raiders piled in.

name: Name
body:
Cynthia quickly regained her footing by slipping into shadow. She came out on the other side to drive a blade up into the jaw of the next ulkor rushing in after Baxter then twirled away to draw a bead on her next target by lifting her rocket launcher. She aimed Past the ulkor’s slumping body at the Jackal now threatening Pokey’s flank. She readied to fire.
Pokey peppered its opponents face with the last rounds of its shield-mounted chain-gun. Each shot produced a hideous, steel-rending screech, the sound that made hardened soldiers grit their teeth. The effect was well worth it, however, as the Jackal was soon overcome, headless and falling over. Pokey’s gun was spent for the attack, left whistling as its chambers spun, sizzling white hot.
The remaining Jackal flailed after Pokey with an outstretched metal claw, but it suddenly found itself unable to stand when Cynthia’s rocket blew its knee out with a timely explosion. It fell to the ground, flailing and crippled, just in time for Pokey to lift a mighty iron-shod foot and stomp the thing to oblivion. Cynthia caught her breath, stepped back to take stock. The last of the raiders in their midst were being beaten back, but this fight was a long way from over.

name: Name
body:
So it had gone, three waves in succession.
Cynthia could see the mighty Orgoth warlord Oriax and retinue on the far side of the river. His arms were crossed expectantly as he waited under his banner. One wave after another he commanded over the bridge to exhaust Cynthia’s defenders. Behind him, another titanic gharlghast awaited its turn with impatience, tugging at the heavy chains that a quartet of ulkor handlers held. Siege tarasks formed a line behind the beast, and Cynthia knew this was to be their final wave.
Yet Oriax would not come yet. The last of the current assault was almost upon them, moving to cross the bridge in a disordered mob. She counted three dozen reavers at least, each armed with curved blades, heavy axes, bolt throwers, or sinister harpoons. By the last two waves, she knew what began as a steady march would soon become a full-scale charge. Fortunately, her Invaders above had kept her platoon supplied. Even now, munitions continued to fall from the sky with marked crates and oversized chutes.

name: Name
body:
As she saw the inbound care packages, a horrible omen appeared to the west of their position. It was an airburst of red smoke, and when she saw it, Cynthia’s resolve faltered for the first time.
"Morrow help us," Baxter said; he’d seen it as well. "They’ve overrun the ruins."
"Keep fighting," Cynthia ordered as she fell to a knee, reloading her rocket launcher out of habit over resolve. Her limbs were tired, her lungs fit to burst.
"How long before they realize we’ve taken what they came for?" Baxter fired his rifle, finishing an ulkor struggling to get up even as he looked to the wave picking up speed over the bridge. "How long before they overrun the city to get it?"
"One thing at a time." Cynthia aimed, sending a rocket screaming downrange and headlong into the reavers. The explosion sent the front rank reeling, two falling dead where they stood. Yet there were too many to come. "For now, we hold the line, Sergeant."
"Yes, ma’am." Baxter was solemn yet resolved.
At least serendipity had not abandoned Cynthia’s platoon. As care packages continued to land from above, Cynthia saw a timely remedy.

name: Name
body:
"Flamethrower," she shouted, compelling Pokey to meet it. Her warjack moved, its ammunition now spent. With three steps forward, Pokey crouched low enough to be serviced by a pair of rangers and waited.
"Get that weapon fitted, double time!" Baxter commanded. It would be double time—or nothing. The reavers had recovered their shock and were still coming—in fact, they were running now, their lusty shouts terrifying.
Four Gravediggers rushed for the marked crate, opened it, and lifted it over the shoulders of Cynthia’s warjack. With practiced ease they locked it in place, and Pokey stood tall again, ready to meet the reaver charge.
For their part, the oncoming reavers either did not sense their peril or did not care. They fell into a wild sprint as Pokey stepped forward to meet them. The igniter at his new weapon’s tapered nozzle sparked, and the taps opened.
Seconds later, the bridge was covered in burning pitch. Pokey heaped gout after gout until the tanks were emptied. In moments, the reavers were fully engulfed, burning and screaming. Then they were dead, scorched and smoking. A cheer went up behind Pokey as Cynthia’s Gravediggers celebrated the end of the third wave. Cynthia raised her arms alongside her troops, but in truth, she didn’t feel it. She looked across the bridge to her foe, and there she saw the death of them all.

name: Name
body:
Oriax stood rooted, unmoved by the inferno or the massacre, his arms still crossed. Behind his prized gharlghast, his siege tarasks, his ulkors, and his reavers, yet another formation of axe-wielding troops now fell in line. The odds were beyond measure, and Cynthia knew it. Though it was far from the first time she had looked death in the face, she felt fatigue seeping into her bones. Perhaps victory was impossible this day. Every soldier knew such a day might find them. All any of them could do was make it count.
As she looked over the remains of her battered platoon, the smouldering bridge beyond their lines and the Orgoth host on the other side of the bridge, she found Oriax staring back at her. With finality, she met his stony gaze and held it. Then she pointed at him, drawing a line across her neck.
Live or die, she aimed to make it so.
It seemed her gesture struck a chord. The warlord reacted at last, uncrossing his arms. Next, he raised one, aimed it toward the bridge, and started walking. Behind him, his army moved to follow. Horns sounded; a roar went up among them.

name: Name
body: Cynthia swallowed hard. It was not the response she had wished for. "Looks like yeh could use a hand, darlin’." The man’s voice came from directly behind her. Not just any man’s voice either. It was a low-born lilt from the north, a whispered gravel as familiar as her own. It was also impossible. On the other hand, it wouldn’t be the first time he’d appeared from out of nowhere. Cynthia turned round, expecting for all the world her mind had been playing tricks on her. Yet there stood her father, Spellstorms drawn. Behind him, the Hellslingers formed a line, silent, ready, and smiling. "Pa—" Cynthia started, her eyes wide with shock. "Major Caine!" "Reporting for duty." "How did yeh?" Cynthia stammered. "I’ll tell yeh all about it, kid." Caine winked as he pointed back to Oriax and the approaching force across the bridge. "Yeh want to kill these bastards first?" "More than anything." Cynthia smiled.
